title: Realtime windowed batcher investigation notes
content:
Context and symptom summary:
- After the 2026-02-20 rollout of the model-switcher change (variant fallback optimization), several production routes saw a ~22% drop in token/sec during peak (observed 09:30-11:00 PST). Non-zero error rates, increased queue latency, and sporadic 95th/99th token-latency spikes.
- Issue seems correlated with continuous-batcher config that uses a 12ms window (window_ms) + dynamic coalescing (max_batch_tokens 4096) for realtime routes.

Timeline of quick experiments (notes + commands tried):
1) 2026-02-24 10:15 — reproduce locally on canary cluster- kubectl -n serving logs deploy/realtime-batcher --tail=200 | grep -i "batch_window"- observed repeated: "batch_window_ms=12 queued=31 coalesced=0" and many "evicted_by_timeout" messages
2) 2026-02-24 10:30 — increase window to 24ms on canary- kubectl -n serving set env deploy/realtime-batcher BATCH_WINDOW_MS=24- result: tokens/sec improved ~9% within 5m, p95 reduced but not back to baseline
3) 2026-02-25 08:40 — roll back model-switcher fallback for one route (route A) via feature-flag- route A tokens/sec returned to ~97% baseline; route B still at -20%
4) 2026-02-26 14:00 — capture detailed trace around KV cache hits/misses- curl -sS http://canary-metrics/api/v1/trace?trace_id=abc123 > trace.log- trace snippets: "kv_cache_lookup=miss metric=hotkey_miss=0.03" and "batch_size=1 latency_ms=42 scheduler_wait_ms=18"

Key log snippets (copied from canary):
- 2026-02-24T10:18:07Z [batcher] WARN evicted_by_timeout user_queue=127 route=rt-A window_ms=12
- 2026-02-24T10:18:07Z [scheduler] INFO schedule_attempt batch_size=1 tokens=24 kernel_hint=gpu_fast
- 2026-02-24T10:18:08Z [runtime] ERROR fallback_kernel cpu_selected=true reason=kernel_compilation_timeout

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Window size too small for shifted request distribution: after model-switcher change some routes now have slightly burstier short requests; continuous batcher often emits tiny singletons because max_wait/ms expiration frequently triggers before coalescing. (evidence: many evicted_by_timeout + batch_size=1 logs)
2) Kernel fallback/compilation latency interacting with batcher: when runtime falls back to CPU or compiles new kernels, per-request latency increases causing scheduler backpressure, which in turn prevents larger batches from forming (evidence: runtime ERROR fallback_kernel messages, spike in scheduler_wait_ms)
3) KV cache prefetch radiating latencies: KV prefetch worker sometimes starves CPU cycles; in low-latency windows this prevents quick coalescing. (evidence weak: small rise in cpu_steal metric during incidents)
4) Autoscaler or pod churn causing transient capacity reduction at peak leading to more singletons and tail latency. (evidence: no restarts recorded in cluster events for impacted period, less likely)

Commands / data pulls used (for reproducibility):
- kubectl -n serving logs deploy/realtime-batcher --since=2h | egrep "batch_window|evicted_by_timeout|batch_size|fallback_kernel"- jq to inspect traces: cat trace.log | jq -r '.spans[] | "{.timestamp} {.attrs.batch_size} {.attrs.scheduler_wait_ms}"'
- grafana query: rate(requests_total{route=~"rt-.*"}[5m]) and histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- curl for internal endpoints: curl -X POST http://canary-ingress/routeA/generate -d @sample-payload.json -H 'x-debug:1' -sS -D - | sed -n '1,120p'

Quick fixes attempted and outcome: (notes)
- bump BATCH_WINDOW_MS from 12->24 on canary: partial improvement but not full recovery (tokens/sec +9%).
- disabled model-switcher fallback on route A: recovery for that route, implies interaction with variant routing.
- temporarily disabled kv-prefetch worker on one node: no measurable improvement (probably not primary).

Next steps (actionable items):
- Run controlled A/B on canary with 12ms vs 36ms vs 60ms windows for 24h to capture distribution changes (owner: Samira).
- Add more fine-grained logs in scheduler to record queue depth at window open/close (owner: Liam).
- Reproduce kernel fallback locally by forcing kernel_version mismatch; capture compilation traces and time to readiness (owner: Diego).
- Add metric: batch_emission_aged (count of batches emitted due to timeout) and expose in per-route dashboard (owner: eng-observability).
- Prepare mitigation: if batch_emission_aged share > 30% then temporarily increase BATCH_WINDOW_MS by +2x and alert on regressions.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Did the model-switcher change alter token length distribution subtly (e.g., more short completions)? Need sampling of input/output lengths pre/post.
- Are there CPU steal/backpressure patterns at node-level at the exact minute of regressions? correlate with node-exporter metrics.
- Is the recent kernel compilation load coming from canary-only builds (CI) that coincide with peak? correlate build schedule with incidents.

Notes to self / reminders: messy logs at 10:18 are gold. Save the full raw logs under /tmp/realtime-batcher-20260224.log and attach to JIRA-INF-2481. When running window experiments, keep client-side request inter-arrival variability (don't synthetic uniform arrival).

Slack references: #runtime-ops thread (link above) — timestamped discussion 2026-02-24 11:05 where Diego suggested looking at BATCH_MAX_TOKENS too.

Rough TL;DR to drop in incident channel: "Investigating throughput regression tied to continuous-batcher timing. Initial signal points to too-small batch window combined with occasional kernel fallbacks causing backpressure -> many singleton batches. Short-term mitigation: increase window on sensitive routes and add emitted-due-to-timeout metric."

TODO (short):
- [ ] Run 36ms, 60ms experiments (Samira)
- [ ] Add batch_emission_aged metric (Liam)
- [ ] Kernel-fallback reproducible trace + timeline (Diego)
- [ ] Collect pre/post model-switcher length histograms (Samira)

End of scratchpad.
